headline: The people of Bangladesh and Portugal have much in common, Princess Maria Francisca says

members.title: Portugal’s Princess Maria Francisca visits Prothom Alo office
members.lead: Portugal’s Princess Infanta Maria Francisca visited the Prothom Alo office on Wednesday (18 November 2026). She was accompanied by her husband, Duarte de Sousa Araújo Martins, and a delegation from London Tea Exchange. Prothom Alo Editor Matiur Rahman welcomed them. A discussion was held on the occasion, covering the historical ties between Bangladesh and Portugal, language, culture, migration, the potential of the tea industry and the social role of the media. The guests were also briefed on Prothom Alo’s activities. They received floral greetings and commemorative gifts.

members.title: The people of Bangladesh and Portugal have much in common, Princess Maria Francisca says
members.lead: There are many similarities between the lifestyles, cultures and values of the people of Bangladesh and Portugal. Greater interaction between the two countries could create opportunities for people to learn a great deal from one another. In particular, European countries need to know more about the abilities and skills of the people of Bangladesh. Princess Infanta Maria Francisca, a member of Portugal’s Royal House of Braganza (Bragança), made these remarks while visiting the Prothom Alo office in Karwan Bazar, Dhaka, on Wednesday. Her husband, Duarte de Sousa Araújo Martins, accompanied her. Prothom Alo Editor Matiur Rahman welcomed them. The members of Portugal’s royal family are visiting Bangladesh at the invitation of London Tea Exchange. As part of their visit, they toured the Prothom Alo office on Wednesday. . Officials of London Tea Exchange said one of the main objectives of the visit was to promote Sylhet tea in the international market. They are also involved in initiatives to strengthen cultural and trade relations between the people of the two countries and ensure fair wages for tea workers. The discussion meeting at the Prothom Alo office covered the historical ties between Bangladesh and Portugal, similarities in language and culture, migration, the potential of the tea industry and the social role of the media. Others attending the meeting included London Tea Exchange Group Chairman Sheikh Aliur Rahman, Director Abdul Mohammad Shalim Mukit, UK-based lawyer Farhan Khan Farani and journalist Mohammad Tahir Chaudhry, among others. Senior members of the Prothom Alo team also took part in the discussion. . At the beginning of the meeting, Prothom Alo Editor Matiur Rahman highlighted several words of Portuguese origin used in the Bengali language. He said many words used in everyday Bengali had similarities with Portuguese. He cited the words ‘girja’, ‘padri’, ‘kamra’ and ‘alkatra’ as examples.
